_readme: The LADDER ledger — for each capability that produces something durable in a founder's project:
what it produces, which rung it belongs to, and what seam it leaves if the project is below that rung.
WHY THIS EXISTS: `boss sync` compared FILE to FILE. It could tell a founder that `.claude/skills/
landing/SKILL.md` changed by 40 lines; it could not tell them that they HAVE a landing page and it is
now behind the practice. Distribution without adoption — every improvement BOSS makes to a capability
was unreachable by everyone who had already used it. And skills themselves read their INPUTS (brand,
tokens, canvas) and never looked for their OUTPUT, so pointing /landing at a repo that already had a
landing page generated a second one.
The discipline is `library/practices/seed-to-scale.md`. This file is its machine-readable half.
rung        Quickstart | MVP | V1 | Scale — where this capability genuinely belongs. NOT where it
ships. /landing ships in MVP mode and its demand-page half belongs at Quickstart; the
rung is about the WORK, not the install.
produces.what  reads in TWO sentences and must work in both: "you already have ___" (sync)
and "Already built: ___" (status). A short noun phrase, not a feature blurb.
produces    what the founder ends up with, and how to look for it. `files` are path patterns
(`*` = one segment, `**` = any depth); `deps` are package.json dependency names.
DELIBERATELY TIGHT. A false 'you already have this' costs more than a miss — the loose
half (a smoke gate called `verify`, a landing page in Framer) is the MODEL's job at
step 0, not a path list's. Same split as detect.js: cheap and legible here, judgment there.
seam        what to plant when the project is BELOW the rung — or null, honestly, when there is
nothing worth planting. A seam is a column, a stub, a folder, or a habit. If it needs a
document, a decision, or a dependency, it is the practice wearing a seam's clothes.
The test: skip this for six months — what is GONE, versus merely UNDONE?
seamNot     the thing it keeps being mistaken for. Present so the boundary can't erode quietly.
A `seam: null` entry is COMPLETE, not unfinished. Most practices cost the same written later, and
inventing a seam to look helpful is how a just-in-time tool turns into a checklist.
Enforced by `npm run check:ladder` — a capability that produces a durable artifact and is missing
here fails BOSS's own build. That gate is what makes this ongoing rather than a one-time sweep.

canvas.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
canvas.seamWhy: There is no rung below this one. The canvas IS the seed.

spec.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
spec.seam: Write down what 'working' means for the feature while you are building it — one sentence, in the commit or a comment. It costs nothing now and it is the only thing that makes a test writable later.
spec.seamNot: A spec convention, an ID scheme, acceptance-criteria fields, a template.
spec.seamWhy: You can write a spec any day. You cannot reconstruct what you MEANT by 'correct' six months after you built it — and an agent asked to test that feature later will happily write assertions against whatever the code already does.

smoke.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
smoke.alsoLookFor: A project can have a smoke gate under another name — a `verify`/`check` make target, a `test` script that actually boots the app, a pre-commit hook. If they have one, the gap is BOSS's blindness, not their discipline; say so and wire to it rather than adding a second.
smoke.seamWhy: A gate costs the same to add later. What is genuinely lost belongs to `spec` above — the criterion, not the runner.

evals.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
evals.appliesWhen: the project has an LLM in control flow
evals.seam: Keep the bad outputs. One folder, paste the failure in, no format. That is eval case #1 and it exists for about thirty seconds before someone closes the tab.
evals.seamNot: An eval harness, a judge, a rubric, a CI gate, a scoring loop.
evals.seamWhy: Every eval set is built from real failures you actually saw. You can write the harness any day; you cannot recover the weird output you deleted, and reproducing it on demand is exactly the thing a non-deterministic system will not do for you.

ai-cost.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
ai-cost.appliesWhen: the project makes its first LLM call
ai-cost.seam: One line per call: model, tokens in/out, timestamp. Append to a file. Nothing reads it yet.
ai-cost.seamNot: A budget, a review cadence, alerts, a dashboard, a per-user attribution scheme.
ai-cost.seamWhy: Same shape as the analytics history seam — you cannot backfill what past calls cost, so the day you finally care about margin, your ledger starts at day zero and the whole build you already paid for is invisible.

ai-failure-states.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
ai-failure-states.appliesWhen: the project makes its first LLM call
ai-failure-states.seamWhy: A failure-state design costs the same written later. The recoverable-only-now half is the specific weird output you saw and closed the tab on — that seam belongs to `evals`, and duplicating it here would be a second ask for the same habit.

ai-first-init.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
ai-first-init.seamWhy: A conductor over capabilities that carry their own seams. It has none of its own, and giving it one would ask for the same thing twice.

design-tokens-init.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
design-tokens-init.seam: Name the first color for what it MEANS, not what it looks like — `action.primary`, not `indigo-600`. One habit, zero files.
design-tokens-init.seamNot: A three-layer token architecture, a Style Dictionary pipeline, a semantic layer, a component library.
design-tokens-init.seamWhy: Nothing is technically lost — but the cost is the only one on this list that compounds per screen. Retrofitting is linear in UI you already generated, and an agent generating screen forty has forty precedents telling it to invent a new blue.

ship.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
ship.seam: Read config from the environment from the first commit — `process.env.X`, even when X is a placeholder you also hardcode nowhere.
ship.seamNot: A host, a pipeline, a rollback runbook, a staging environment, secret management.
ship.seamWhy: A key committed once is in git history forever. Moving it to `.env` later does not remove it — it is a rotate-and-purge job, not an edit, and this is the signature vibe-coded leak (CVE-2025-48757 / MoltBook). The one-way door here is not the deploy, it is the history.

landing.stepZeroMarker: Step 0a — does a page already exist?
landing.rungNote: The PRODUCT page is MVP. The DEMAND page is Quickstart — that is /pretotype's fake door, and it is the rung below.
landing.alsoLookFor: A landing page often lives OUTSIDE the repo — Framer, Carrd, Webflow, a Notion page, a GitHub Pages branch. Ask before generating; a page you cannot see is still a page they have.
landing.seam: If anything of yours is public — a page, a repo, a post — leave one way for a stranger to reach you. An email field, a link, anything.
landing.seamNot: A landing page, a waitlist product, a CRM, an email tool, a form service, copy.
landing.seamWhy: You can rewrite a page any day. You cannot go back and ask the people who already showed up and left — and at this rung those are the only people who found you without being told to.

measure.stepZeroMarker: First, look for what's already there.
measure.rungNote: Genuinely post-first-users. Below ~10 users the honest answer is 'go talk to them', which /measure says itself.
measure.seam: A `created_at` on user rows and core object rows, plus one `track(event, props)` that console-logs and goes nowhere.
measure.seamNot: An event taxonomy, a tool account, a dashboard, an `events` table, a funnel.
measure.seamWhy: The history seam — the only thing on this entire ladder that gets strictly more expensive every single day it is skipped. You can add a tracking call any day; you cannot add the past. Full treatment in analytics-for-ai-products.md § 'But leave the seam'.

onboard.stepZeroMarker: you cannot re-hear someone's first five minutes
onboard.rungNote: The top-of-curve fix /health routes to. Needs real users to have a curve at all.
onboard.seam: When one of your first ten users tries the thing, write down what they actually said and where they stalled. Their words, not your summary.
onboard.seamNot: An onboarding flow, a checklist, a product tour, a concierge process, an aha-moment definition.
onboard.seamWhy: You can redesign onboarding any day. You cannot re-hear someone's first five minutes — and after their second session they are no longer a person who has never seen your product, so that observation is unrepeatable by construction.

money.stepZeroMarker: say a number out loud and watch the face
money.rungNote: Not a mode so much as an event: someone said yes.
money.seam: In any conversation you are already having, say a number out loud and watch the face.
money.seamNot: An entity, a payment rail, a pricing page, ToS, a billing system, a refund policy.
money.seamWhy: You will talk to a finite number of early users and each one is a single-use willingness-to-pay probe. Every conversation you finish without naming a price is a data point you cannot re-collect — going back later to ask changes the question, because by then they know you.

trust.stepZeroMarker: turn on your model provider's training opt-out
trust.rungNote: Fires when real users' real data arrives, which can be well before V1 by mode.
trust.seam: Two acts, both one-time. Don't store what no feature reads. And turn on your model provider's training opt-out — in the console, today.
trust.seamNot: A privacy policy, ToS, a subprocessor list, a trust page, a DPIA, SOC2.
trust.seamWhy: Both are one-way doors and neither is a document. You cannot un-collect data, and a policy written later cannot cover what you already gathered under no policy at all. You cannot un-train a model on prompts you already sent — the opt-out is an ACT, not a promise, and 'the AI did it' has already failed as a defense (Air Canada).

design-library.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
design-library.seamWhy: It costs the same at V1 as it would have at MVP, minus the components that did not exist yet. The rung below it is the tokens file, and that seam is already `design-tokens-init`'s.

incident.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?
incident.seam: Log errors with a timestamp somewhere you can read later. Not a service — a file is fine.
incident.seamNot: A runbook, an on-call rotation, an SLO, alerting, a status page, a postmortem template.
incident.seamWhy: A runbook genuinely costs the same written later, and pretending otherwise would be ceremony. But you cannot investigate an outage you have no record of, and the first real one is exactly when you find out which it was.

_why: Skills that produce NOTHING a founder would later want updated. Every skill in every stage
manifest must be in this list or in the ladder above — `npm run check:ladder` fails otherwise.
That is the forcing function: a new capability cannot ship without someone deciding which it is.
The test is APPEND-ONLY vs DURABLE. A DEC-NNN, an EVID-NNN, a devlog entry — each run writes a
NEW record and never revisits an old one, so "do you already have one?" is not a question that
means anything. A landing page, a schema, a privacy policy — one exists, and the next run should
read it. If you are unsure, ask whether a founder would ever say "update mine" rather than
"make another"; if they would, it belongs in the ladder.
_exempt.boss: the entry point; captures an idea into a new IDEA-NNN record
_exempt.boss-learn: BOSS's own learning loop, not a project artifact
_exempt.boss-sync: BOSS's own distribution loop, not a project artifact
_exempt.comprehend: the assessor itself — reads the repo, never produces a competing artifact
_exempt.triage: routes an input to the right verb
_exempt.import: pulls source material in; the source is the founder's, not BOSS's output
_exempt.decide: append-only record (DEC-NNN) — every run adds one, never updates an existing
_exempt.close: session ritual; updates RESUME, which is BOSS's own convention not a founder artifact
_exempt.prototype: throwaway by design — a prototype you'd 'update' has stopped being one
_exempt.pretotype: the fake door is deliberately disposable; its durable half is /landing
_exempt.consult: advisory only — mentors never write product code
_exempt.extract: routes a pattern UP or DOWN; the record is append-only
_exempt.revalidate: a gate; the output is a routing decision
_exempt.cost-review: a reader over the cost ledger; the review file is append-only
_exempt.roadmap: explicitly a snapshot you use and discard, never a plan you tend
_exempt.board: a reader over the project's own files
_exempt.design-review: a check over an existing design
_exempt.ux-check: a check over an existing flow

comp-eval.stepZeroMarker: ## Step 0 — does it already exist, and is this the right rung?

produces.what: the competitive field — a living set of rivals with sources and checked dates

comp-eval.seam: When you notice a rival, write the name, what you saw, and TODAY'S DATE — one line, anywhere in docs/. That's it.
comp-eval.seamWhy: Durable, and unusually so: the value is the DRIFT — what a rival charged in March versus what they charge now. The survey can always be run later; the observation cannot be recovered, because a pricing page carries no history and the Wayback Machine is not a plan. So the seam is the dated one-liner, and nothing more — a Quickstart founder who starts maintaining a matrix has taken on the practice two rungs early, which is the failure this boundary exists to prevent.
comp-eval.seamNot: A competition folder, a comparison table, a feature matrix, pricing research, a file per rival, or a survey of the field.
